text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Amid Japanese fears that two of its car makers with plants in Australia - Toyota and Mitsubishi - would be disadvantaged by further reductions in protection, Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto is expected to raise reservations about the prospect of further cuts in Australian car tariffs when he meets Prime Minister John Howard today. Page 1.

The directors of bancassurance giant Colonial Ltd CGH.AX surprised the investment community yesterday when it closed its public share offer at midday, four days earlier than planned, following unexpectedly strong demand from retail investors. Colonial will be the second of Australia's three big insurance groups to list on the Australian Stock Exchange. Page 1.

Lion Nathan chief executive Doug Myers acknowledged yesterday the brewing company had had one of its toughest periods in its 140-year history, revealing it had reported a 20 per cent fall in interim earnings to NZ$72.2 million, and had suffered a 10 per cent drop in pre-tax earnings from its Australian operations to A$110.53 million. Page 21.

The board of Australian National Industries Ltd will not yet respond to a report by Bob Ellicot QC into ANI's acquisition of German environmental engineering business ABT from Kerry Packer as it is awaiting a request for further information. Page 22.

Shell Australia has fallen into line with Ampol, BP and Mobil with a 30 per cent drop in profit to A$277 million last year, and has backed its oil industry colleagues' attack on the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, with Shell chairman and cief executive officer Roland Williams warning that at least one of the country's four refining companies would be forced to close if the regulation controlling the industry remained. Page 23.

Just months after its US-based parent, United International Holdings, abandoned a US$250 million capital raising, regional pay-TV operator Austar announced yesterday it had finalised a A$200 million bank facility designed to carry the company through unti it begins to make profits in 1999. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Colonial Ltd CGH.AX managing director Peter Smedley told a Securities Institute lunch in Melbourne yesterday the bancassurance group will list on the stock market on May 12 - a week earlier than planned - after yesterday closing its public share offer four days head of schedule amid strong support for its A$2 billion float. Page 21.

Pay-TV operator Austar has won a crucial A$200 million performance-based debt facility with the Chase Manhattan Bank to help it complete its ambitious pay-TV rollout in regional and remote Australia. Under the deal, Austar would be expected to almost doube its existing subscriber base to 360,000 if it wanted to draw down the entire A$200 million facility. Page 21.

Announcing a 30.5 per cent profit drop to A$277 million for 1996, Shell Australia chairman Roland Williams warned yesterday the company would not continue to carry its A$2 billion retail petrol division if operating profits did not improve, saying the indstry would experience pain through restructure. Page 23.

Base metals giant MIM Holdings Ltd has attributed falls in its third-quarter production of silver, lead, zinc and copper to extremely wet weather and a 25-day shutdown of its copper Isa-smelt smelter. The three months to March 31 saw copper anode production fall 30.2 per cent to 28,460 tonnes. Page 23.

Speaking at the 10th Metal Bulletin International Iron Ore Symposium in Berlin yesterday, West Australian Resources Minister Colin Barnett predicted Australia's unprocessed iron ore exports would peak at about 200 million tonnes a year thanks to the growth of new steel-making technologies. Page 23.

North Ltd managing director Campbell Anderson has reversed the company's earlier expectations of flat full-year earnings after improvements at its zinc operations in Sweden, higher uranium sales, and its recently purchased iron-ore operations in Canada cotributed to a strong third-quarter profit of A$39.2 million. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Brewing group Lion Nathan is confident of posting a stronger performance in the last half of 1997, despite posting a 20.8 per cent slump in net profit in the six months to February 28 following a further fall in Australian market share and profits, and a significant drop in New Zealand volumes. Page 29.

In a move suggesting its A$1.6 billion float will be priced at the top end of expectations, giving bigger gains for its 700,000 small investors, Colonial Ltd CGH.AX yesterday closed its public share offer four days early after being swamped with applications. Mihael Heffernan, of broker FW Holst, said he thought the unusual decision was an Australian first. Page 29.

Addressing a public meeting of more than 100 affected investors in Adelaide yesterday, RetireInvest managing director Tony Muston offered full compensation to South Australian retiree clients who have suffered losses of an estimated A$10 million to A$20 mllion from unauthorised share trading involving the company. Page 29.

The Australian National Industries board yesterday received a report by Bob Ellicot QC on its controversial purchase of German waste-to-energy business ABT from Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press Holdings, but declined to reveal whether it would release the document to shareholders. Page 29.

Optus Communications chief Ziggy Switkowski, who was at the centre of the company's decision to move to total ownership of Optus Vision, believes a cable-sharing deal with Telstra can be easily reached, but says a wider restructuring of the pay-TV industry will be much harder to achieve. Page 31.

AMP Investments managing director Leigh Hall yesterday outlined a strategy with will see the AMP Society's investment division become a quasi merchant bank within a few years by helping to fund the expansion of Australian companies overseas. The plan is amed at expanding AMP's direct investment portfolio, which has posted a return of 10.7 per cent in the past decade. Page 31.
THE AGE

In a move that underscores Pacific Dunlop's Ansell group as the PacDun's growth centre, Ansell has paid A$115 million for US-based glove maker Golden Needles Knitting Inc, boosting its strong ranking in global industrial gloves products and clearing the wy for Ansell to extend its sales in Europe. Page B1.

Following reports that it plans to drastically reduce its 82-year-old Newcastle steelworks and be out of the industry by 2020, BHP was threatened yesterday with major industrial action and was attacked by Labor MPs, who called on the Big Australian to leave the steel-making business immediately and allow in new competitors rather than let the industry deteriorate in the next 25 years. Page B1.

Peter Mitchell, a former Bond group director in charge of corporate planning and development, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court yesterday to playing a significant role in Australia's biggest corporate fraud - the stripping of A$1 billion in cash from Bell Resources in the late 1980s. Page B1.

In a surprise decision which means investors planning last-minute applications have missed out, banking and insurance giant Colonial yesterday closed its public share offer early - the original closing date was this Friday - after it was swamped with applcations. Colonial's listing date has also been brought forward to May 12. Page B1.

Pacific Dunlop's legal problems in North America have broadened beyond its heart pacemaker litigation, with the group's Ansell division now a co-respondent in 33 cases, 15 of which are Federal actions, in the United States, resulting from hyperallergic rections to latex medical examination gloves. Page B1.

According to a survey of 287 expatriate executives living in countries across East Asia by Hong Kong-based research company Political and Economic Risk Consultancy, Malaysia has overtaken Singapore and Thailand as the place most expatriate businessmen woud prefer to live in Asia - but Australia still outshines all the Asian countries for quality of life and amenities. Page B1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
